chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:

“An elderly person and one afflicted with chronic thirst are under no hardship if they break their fast in the Month of Ramadan. Each one of them should give a mudd of food in charity for every day, and there is no make-up fast upon them. If they are unable, then there is nothing upon them.”

key_terms.الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ: an aged elderly person whose condition prevents normal fasting
key_terms.الْعُطَاشُ: chronic thirst or a persistent condition of excessive thirst
key_terms.بِمُدٍّ: a mudd, a specific measure of food given as charity
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month in which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِمَا: no further obligation is due from them
key_terms.يُفْطِرَا: to break or not observe the fast

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an elderly person or someone with chronic thirst who cannot fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for an elderly person and a person suffering from chronic thirst who cannot endure fasting in Ramadan. They may break the fast and give a mudd of food for each day, with no qada' required; if even that is beyond their ability, then no liability remains upon them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1947 - Al-'Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

'An elderly person and one suffering from chronic thirst are not at fault if they break their fast during the Month of Ramadan. Each of them should give a mudd (a specific measure) of food as charity for each day, and there is no obligation to make up the fast. If they cannot afford this, then there is nothing upon them.'"
